lock_findings: cached() validates the existing descriptor as an owner-only regular single-link inode, then takes the lock before seal::verified. hint_file is try_clone of that file, and open_database consumes the original File directly in builder.create_file; there is no unlock, pathname reopen or ownership gap.

The macOS lock is F_OFD_SETLK/F_WRLCK with SEEK_SET, zero start and zero length, covering current contents and future growth. EINTR is retried; EAGAIN/EACCES becomes DatabaseAlreadyOpen; other syscall failures propagate.

Linux and other non-macOS branches preserve the prior File::try_lock and exact WouldBlock/error mapping. No integrity check, source stamp, row fingerprint, deadline repair callback or original receipt check was removed.

The new real database test tries independent open file descriptions before open, after redb takes ownership, and after commit; it requires exclusion and verifies a real write/read after owned descriptors are released.
platform_findings: Directory::create/open/verify reject non-Linux before any mkdirat, adoption or identity traversal. Directory::remove first calls verify. Scratch::create rejects before adoption can write claim.json; ScratchOwner::prepare delegates first to Directory::create.
stop_original_group rejects non-Linux before /proc inspection and before the first numeric process-group signal.

jobctl start/pty reject before policy/lock/registry creation. supervise rejects before signal installation or spec/state reads. The top-level dispatcher only checks arguments, credentials, bounded input and ID before these calls.

Original Linux positive test functions remain. Added non-Linux tests verify unchanged directories/sentinels and a live owned child after refusal; they then clean up that child themselves. These negative tests do not claim successful engines or isolated launch on macOS.
